title: The Little Pebble's Big Roll
markdown:
Luna the lamb and Muffin the marmot were getting ready for sleep. Their day had been hops and looking and a story about sleepy owls. Now the world was going quiet. Time to rest.

Luna's wool was as soft and white as a little cloud. She was cozy in her meadow bed. Clover drifted on the air, sweet. Muffin, whiskers twitching, was snuggled in his warm burrow, earthy and snug.

But wait. What was that little rustle?

Out in the garden, moonlight made shiny patterns on the sleepy leaves. A little pebble — a smooth friend who usually sat on the path by the big rose bush — had rolled just a tiny bit away. He liked his spot. He liked the solid path and his pebble pals. Tonight he felt a little lonely. A little wobbly. Not in his special place.

Luna's soft lashes blinked. "Muffin," she whispered, "look. Our little pebble seems out of place. He looks as if he has lost his way a little bit."

Muffin was about to yawn a rumble that could almost shake the leaves, but only almost. He opened one sleepy bright eye. "Oh my goodness. A little pebble problem. A little rolling riddle!"

The pebble felt them looking kindly. He gave a tiny silent wobble. He missed the firm path. He missed his friends.

"Don't you worry one bit, little pebble friend," called Luna, like a lullaby. "We'll help you back. We'll be your gentle guides."

Muffin nodded. His whiskery smile wiggled. "A gentle push, a little nudge, and home you go. Faster than a sleepy bee flies to a flower — but slower, really. Slow is the point."

Luna walked over. Soft hooves, no sound on the dewy grass. Muffin followed. Scritch-scratch went his paws, a gentle drum. The pebble was smooth and round, still warm from the sun that had gone to bed behind the hills.

"Now, little pebble," whispered Luna. She nudged him with her fluffy head, soft as a fallen feather. "A little roll, a little sway."

Muffin added a warm rumble. "No bumps, no bounces. Just smooth rolling for our friend."

A little roll, a little sway,
slowly, slowly, on your way.

Luna's nose: a breath of encouragement. Muffin's paw: a touch as light as a snowflake. The pebble began to roll, ever so slowly, ever so gently, as if he floated on a tiny cloud. They rolled past sleepy daisies, petals curled up for the night. They rolled past a snail who was already a little house, and the snail did not even wake. They rolled past moonlit blades of grass that shimmered like tiny green jewels. The journey was so calm, so quiet. No loud noises. No sudden surprises. Just the soft rustle of leaves whispering secrets to the night wind, and the gentle reassuring whispers of Luna and Muffin, and the song:

A little roll, a little sway,
slowly, slowly, on your way.

"We're almost there," Muffin rumbled, cozy as a blanket. "A few more little rolls. A gentle roll and a happy sigh."

"Feel the path getting closer?" Luna's voice was a sweet line. "It's waiting."

One last super-gentle nudge from Luna. One soft tender pat from Muffin. The pebble rolled into his perfect spot. A happy soft little thump. The familiar path. Home. The other pebbles nearby seemed to smile in the moonlight, which pebbles do by simply being round.

Luna and Muffin watched. The pebble looked snug, a little island of peace.

"There we go," whispered Luna. "All snuggled in."

Muffin yawned, big and wide, and stretched. "That was a very important job. Now our own cozy beds, don't you think?"

They padded back. Moonlight like a friendly lantern. Luna snuggled into meadow wool. Muffin burrowed deeper, warm as always.

The little pebble on the garden path felt the firm place under him. He did not need a speech. He had the path. He had his pals. He had the last of the sun's warmth, fading.

A little roll, a little sway,
home at last, and here you'll stay.

Soon the moonbeams watched Luna, and Muffin, and the happy little pebble, and the garden went on being a garden, quiet enough for three kinds of sleep.
